### stackTraceLimit [#stacktracelimit]

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

Defined in: node\_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.6.2/node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from [#inherited-from-3]

`Error.stackTraceLimit`

## Methods [#methods]

### captureStackTrace() [#capturestacktrace]

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Defined in: node\_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.6.2/node\_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters [#parameters-1]

##### targetObject [#targetobject]

`object`

##### constructorOpt? [#constructoropt]

`Function`

#### Returns [#returns-1]

`void`

#### Inherited from [#inherited-from-4]

`Error.captureStackTrace`

# createPatchableTravels() (/docs/api-reference/functions/createPatchableTravels)

## Call Signature [#call-signature]

Defined in: [src/createPatchableTravels.ts:11](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/createPatchableTravels.ts#L11)

Create a Travels instance whose state is statically constrained to the
durable JSON-shaped subset supported by patches and persistence.

### Returns [#returns]

#### getRevision() [#getrevision]

> `readonly` **getRevision**: () => `number`

Monotonic token for committed observable timeline transitions.

##### Returns [#returns-1]

`number`

#### getState() [#getstate]

> `readonly` **getState**: () => `S`

Borrowed live state, the same value observers receive as `event.state`.

##### Returns [#returns-2]

`S`

##### Remarks [#remarks]

Typed as `S` so it can flow into stores and APIs that expect the state
type, but it must be treated as read-only: history patches apply to this
value, so mutating it outside Travels operations desynchronizes undo/redo.
In immutable mode its objects are also the values of retained patches, so
such a mutation rewrites the history that redo replays.
`enableAutoFreeze` freezes every state Travels produces after creation.

#### mutable [#mutable]

> `readonly` **mutable**: `boolean`

> **createPatchableTravels**\<`S`, `F`, `P`\>(`initialState`, `options`): [`Travels`](../type-aliases/Travels.mdx)\<`S`, `F`, `false`, `P`\>

# createTravels() (/docs/api-reference/functions/createTravels)

Create a new Travels instance

## Call Signature [#call-signature]

> **createTravels**\<`S`, `F`, `P`\>(`initialState`, `options?`): `object`

Defined in: [src/createTravels.ts:8](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/createTravels.ts#L8)

Create a new Travels instance with auto archive mode

### Type Parameters [#type-parameters]

#### S [#s]

`S`

#### F [#f]

`F` *extends* `boolean` = `false`

#### P [#p]

`P` *extends* `object` = \{ \}

### Parameters [#parameters]

#### initialState [#initialstate]

`S`

#### options? [#options]

`Omit`\<[`TravelsOptions`](../type-aliases/TravelsOptions.mdx)\<`F`, `true`, `P`, `S`\>, `"autoArchive"`\> & `object`

### Returns [#returns]

#### getRevision() [#getrevision]

> `readonly` **getRevision**: () => `number`

Monotonic token for committed observable timeline transitions.

##### Returns [#returns-1]

`number`

#### getState() [#getstate]

> `readonly` **getState**: () => `S`

Borrowed live state, the same value observers receive as `event.state`.

##### Returns [#returns-2]

`S`

##### Remarks [#remarks]

Typed as `S` so it can flow into stores and APIs that expect the state
type, but it must be treated as read-only: history patches apply to this
value, so mutating it outside Travels operations desynchronizes undo/redo.
In immutable mode its objects are also the values of retained patches, so
such a mutation rewrites the history that redo replays.
`enableAutoFreeze` freezes every state Travels produces after creation.

#### mutable [#mutable]

> `readonly` **mutable**: `boolean`

#### subscribe() [#subscribe]

# validateTravelHistoryEntry() (/docs/api-reference/functions/validateTravelHistoryEntry)

> **validateTravelHistoryEntry**\<`P`\>(`entry`): \{ `error`: `string`; \} \| \{ `entry`: [`TravelHistoryEntry`](../type-aliases/TravelHistoryEntry.mdx)\<`P`\>; `error`: `null`; \}

Defined in: [src/persistence.ts:232](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/persistence.ts#L232)

Validate and normalize one externally supplied forward/inverse patch pair.
Accessor-backed or inherited fields are rejected without being evaluated.
Use `assertTravelHistoryEntryRecordable()` to also apply the detached-value
rules of `recordPatches()`.

## Most-used exports [#most-used-exports]

| Export | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`createTravels()`](/docs/api-reference/functions/createTravels) | Function | Create a state-owning timeline. |
| [`createPatchableTravels()`](/docs/api-reference/functions/createPatchableTravels) | Function | Create a timeline with durable-input constraints. |
| [`createTravelJournal()`](/docs/api-reference/functions/createTravelJournal) | Function | Create an externally owned controlled journal. |
| [`restoreTravels()`](/docs/api-reference/functions/restoreTravels) | Function | Restore one complete state-owning snapshot. |
| [`restoreTravelJournal()`](/docs/api-reference/functions/restoreTravelJournal) | Function | Restore one complete controlled journal snapshot. |
| [`Travels`](/docs/api-reference/variables/Travels) | Namespace value | Decode persisted input with `Travels.deserialize()`. |
| [`TravelsOptions`](/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/TravelsOptions) | Type | Configure history, ownership, Mutative behavior, and hooks. |
| [`TravelsEvent`](/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/TravelsEvent) | Type | Consume committed subscriber and devtools events. |
| [`TravelsSerializedHistory`](/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/TravelsSerializedHistory) | Type | Store and migrate versioned snapshots. |
| [`TravelsControls`](/docs/api-reference/interfaces/TravelsControls) | Interface | Expose read-only navigation and history controls. |
| [`TravelsPersistenceError`](/docs/api-reference/classes/TravelsPersistenceError) | Class | Handle stable persistence failure codes. |
| [`TRAVELS_HISTORY_SCHEMA_VERSION`](/docs/api-reference/variables/TRAVELS_HISTORY_SCHEMA_VERSION) | Variable | Construct and migrate current-schema snapshots. |

## Reference conventions [#reference-conventions]

- “Defined in” links point to the exact source revision used to generate the page.
- Read-only return objects are capabilities, not constructor-based class instances.
- `Travels` the exported value is a persistence namespace; `Travels<...>` the type describes a state-owning timeline.
- Event names are open to future minor releases; keep a `default` branch in application switches.
- Patch and state views described as read-only must not be cast and mutated. Use the corresponding detached snapshot API.

# PatchableInput<T> (/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/PatchableInput)

> **PatchableInput**\<`T`\> = \[`NonPatchableValue`\<`T`\>\] *extends* \[`never`\] ? `T` : `never`

Defined in: [src/type.ts:160](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/type.ts#L160)

Preserve an inferred state type when its reachable properties are
statically compatible with the durable patch/persistence contract.

Recursive types are inspected to a finite depth and broad `{}`-shaped
values cannot be proven from their static type alone. The strict factory
therefore also validates the concrete initial value at runtime.

## Type Parameters [#type-parameters]

### T [#t]

`T`

# RebasableManualTravelsControls<S, P> (/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/RebasableManualTravelsControls)

> **RebasableManualTravelsControls**\<`S`, `P`\> = [`ManualTravelsControls`](../interfaces/ManualTravelsControls.mdx)\<`S`, `P`\> & `object`

Defined in: [src/type.ts:484](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/type.ts#L484)

## Type Declaration [#type-declaration]

### rebase() [#rebase]

> `readonly` **rebase**: () => `void`

Remove all history and make the current state as the new initial state.

#### Returns [#returns]

`void`

#### Remarks [#remarks]

**IMPORTANT**: This is a destructive operation. All previous and future history entries are discarded,
and the current state (including any unarchived temp patches) becomes the new baseline (position 0). Any subsequent `reset()`
calls will return to this new baseline, not the original initial state.

## Type Parameters [#type-parameters]

### S [#s]

`S`

### P [#p]

`P` *extends* [`PatchesOption`](PatchesOption.mdx) = \{ \}

# RestoreTravelsOptions<S, F, A, P> (/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/RestoreTravelsOptions)

> **RestoreTravelsOptions**\<`S`, `F`, `A`, `P`\> = [`TravelsOptions`](TravelsOptions.mdx)\<`F`, `A`, `P`, `S`\> & `object`

Defined in: [src/restoreTravels.ts:20](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/restoreTravels.ts#L20)

Options accepted by `restoreTravels()`.

The restored state is detached from the snapshot. A mutable timeline can
instead restore into an existing live root, such as a MobX, Vue, or Pinia
store object: Travels overwrites `target` in place with the snapshot state
and keeps that reference as its state.

## Type Declaration [#type-declaration]

### target? [#target]

> `optional` **target**: `S`

Live mutable root that receives the restored state in place. Requires
`mutable: true` and the same plain object or array root kind as the
snapshot state.

## Type Parameters [#type-parameters]

### S [#s]

`S`

### F [#f]

`F` *extends* `boolean`

### A [#a]

`A` *extends* `boolean`

### P [#p]

`P` *extends* [`PatchesOption`](PatchesOption.mdx) = \{ \}

# TravelJournal<S, F, A, P> (/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/TravelJournal)

> **TravelJournal**\<`S`, `F`, `A`, `P`\> = `Readonly`\<`Pick`\<[`Travels`](Travels.mdx)\<`S`, `F`, `A`, `P`\>, `"subscribe"` \| `"getState"` \| `"getRevision"` \| `"getHistory"` \| `"getHistorySnapshot"` \| `"go"` \| `"back"` \| `"forward"` \| `"reset"` \| `"rebase"` \| `"canBack"` \| `"canForward"` \| `"getPosition"` \| `"getPatches"` \| `"serialize"` \| `"assertPersistenceCompatible"` \| `"getMetadata"` \| `"getHistoryEntries"`\> & `object` & `A` *extends* `false` ? `object` : `object`\>

Defined in: [src/createTravelJournal.ts:27](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/createTravelJournal.ts#L27)

Public surface for a timeline whose state is owned by another runtime.

State-owning methods such as `setState()`, transactions, tracking controls,
and `getControls()` are intentionally excluded. External commits enter
through `recordPatches()`; navigation and reset leave through `apply`.

## Type Parameters [#type-parameters]

### S [#s]

`S`

### F [#f]

`F` *extends* `boolean` = `false`

### A [#a]

`A` *extends* `boolean` = `true`

### P [#p]

`P` *extends* [`PatchesOption`](PatchesOption.mdx) = \{ \}

# Travels<S, _F, A, P> (/docs/api-reference/type-aliases/Travels)

> **Travels**\<`S`, `_F`, `A`, `P`\> = `object` & `A` *extends* `false` ? `object` : `object`

Defined in: [src/travels.ts:100](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/blob/5b79ab071f0129c7c1248a058104f08217dcfe6e/src/travels.ts#L100)

Public state-owning Travels capability surface.

Controlled journals expose `recordPatches()` through `TravelJournal`
instead. Manual archive methods exist only when `A` is `false`, keeping
unavailable operations out of both the type and runtime surface.

`_F` records the factory's `enableAutoFreeze` literal. No member depends on
it, but it keeps its position so `Travels<S, false>` cannot silently start
meaning a manual-archive timeline.

## Type Declaration [#type-declaration]

### getRevision() [#getrevision]

> `readonly` **getRevision**: () => `number`

Monotonic token for committed observable timeline transitions.

#### Returns [#returns]

`number`

### getState() [#getstate]

> `readonly` **getState**: () => `S`

Borrowed live state, the same value observers receive as `event.state`.

#### Returns [#returns-1]

`S`

#### Remarks [#remarks]

Typed as `S` so it can flow into stores and APIs that expect the state
type, but it must be treated as read-only: history patches apply to this
value, so mutating it outside Travels operations desynchronizes undo/redo.
In immutable mode its objects are also the values of retained patches, so
such a mutation rewrites the history that redo replays.
`enableAutoFreeze` freezes every state Travels produces after creation.

### mutable [#mutable]

> `readonly` **mutable**: `boolean`

`void`

# History Lifecycle (/docs/concepts/history-lifecycle)

A Travels timeline has two related but different ideas: the **retained history window** used by navigation, and the **instance baseline** used by `reset()`. Understanding their lifecycle prevents subtle undo/redo bugs.

## Positions and entries [#positions-and-entries]

Position `0` is the start of the current retained window. Each patch entry represents a transition to the next position. If three entries are retained, four states can be reconstructed: the window baseline plus three transitions.

```ts
const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 }, { maxHistory: 3 });

for (let index = 0; index < 5; index += 1) {
  travels.setState((draft) => { draft.count += 1; });
}

travels.getState();        // { count: 5 }
travels.getPosition();     // 3
travels.getHistory().map((state) => state.count); // [2, 3, 4, 5]
```

The oldest transitions were trimmed, but the current state remains `5` and the retained window starts at `2`.

## `maxHistory` [#maxhistory]

`maxHistory` must be a non-negative integer. Invalid values such as decimals, `NaN`, and `Infinity` are rejected immediately.

- It counts patch entries, not states.
- Old entries are dropped automatically.
- The position is relative to the retained window and capped at the limit.
- `reset()` can still restore the original instance baseline.
- Use a deliberate limit; “unlimited” history is not a safe persistence strategy by default.

`onWarning` can report `HISTORY_TRIMMED` when the application needs diagnostics. Do not infer overflow solely by comparing positions across every operation; navigation and rebase also change positions.

## `reset()` [#reset]

`reset()` restores the baseline captured when the instance was created or restored, then clears the timeline back to that baseline.

```ts
travels.reset();
console.log(travels.getPosition()); // 0
```

For a restored instance, the baseline is the validated starting timeline captured by the restore operation. Subsequent baseline-changing operations—such as `rebase()`, `replaceStateWithoutHistory()`, or updates while tracking is paused—affect what later resets return to.

## `rebase()` [#rebase]

`rebase()` makes current state the new initial baseline and discards all retained past and future entries.

```ts
travels.rebase();
// reset() now returns to this new baseline.
```

<Callout type="warn" title="Rebase is destructive">
Use `rebase()` only when the old timeline should become unreachable, such as after accepting a server snapshot or deliberately starting a new editing session. It is not the same as undoing to position `0`.
</Callout>

## Creating a new branch [#creating-a-new-branch]

After `back()`, future entries remain available through `forward()` until a new edit commits. That edit discards the redo branch and appends a new entry at the current position.

```ts
const travels = createTravels({ value: 'A' });
travels.setState({ value: 'B' });
travels.setState({ value: 'C' });
travels.back();                  // B, C is redoable
travels.setState({ value: 'D' }); // C is discarded

travels.canForward(); // false
```

Use `onBranchDiscard({ position, discarded })` for auditing or cleanup. The hook runs after the committed transition and cannot veto it.

## Loading state without history [#loading-state-without-history]

`replaceStateWithoutHistory(updater)` applies an update, clears history, and makes the result the new baseline. It is useful for accepting an authoritative remote snapshot or replacing a document without letting users undo into the previous document.

`pauseTracking()` and `resumeTracking()` instead form a scope for updates that should become the new baseline while ordinary timeline operations continue afterward. See [Tracking and Replacement](/docs/guides/tracking-and-replacement).

## Reading history safely [#reading-history-safely]

- `getHistory()` returns a shared, cached, read-only array of read-only state views. Use it while rendering or measuring the current timeline.
- `getHistorySnapshot()` returns detached, caller-owned states. Use it when retaining, sorting, posting to a worker, or mutating the result.
- `getPatches()` returns a detached retained patch snapshot.
- `getControls().patches` is a cached read-only view whose identity remains stable until history changes.

Mutable timelines can share the live object with history entries, so an old `getHistory()` result can reflect later in-place updates. Detached snapshots are the correct tool when historical values must remain fixed.


# How Travels Works (/docs/concepts/how-it-works)

Travels turns each effective update into an immutable state transition plus two patch groups: one that moves forward and one that restores the previous state. The retained sequence of those transitions is the history.

## The five core terms [#the-five-core-terms]

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **State** | The application data at the current timeline position. |
| **Draft** | The mutation-friendly draft passed to a `setState()` recipe. |
| **Patches** | JSON Patch operations describing a transition, plus their inverse. |
| **Position** | The cursor in the retained history window; `0` is its baseline. |
| **Archive** | The act of committing pending changes as a history entry. |

## One edit, two directions [#one-edit-two-directions]

Consider this state and update:

```ts
const travels = createTravels({ title: 'Draft', views: 0 });

travels.setState((draft) => {
  draft.title = 'Published';
  draft.views += 1;
});
```

Conceptually, Travels retains a forward entry like this:

```json
[
  { "op": "replace", "path": "/title", "value": "Published" },
  { "op": "replace", "path": "/views", "value": 1 }
]
```

It also retains the inverse entry needed to restore `{ title: 'Draft', views: 0 }`. `back()` applies inverse operations; `forward()` reapplies forward operations. You do not write either patch group yourself when using `setState()`.

```text
Baseline ── edit A ── edit B ── edit C
   0          1          2          3
                         ▲
                      position
```

Moving back changes the cursor and state; it does not destroy future entries until a new committed edit creates a branch.

## Immutable mode by default [#immutable-mode-by-default]

In the default mode, Travels produces a new immutable state through Mutative. Unchanged branches can be structurally shared. Treat values returned by `getState()`, `getHistory()`, and observer events as read-only: direct writes bypass patch recording and can also modify objects retained by patch values.

Use `enableAutoFreeze: true` in immutable mode when you want accidental writes to fail during development. For a caller-owned history array, use `getHistorySnapshot()` rather than modifying the shared `getHistory()` cache.

## Mutable mode for identity-stable stores [#mutable-mode-for-identity-stable-stores]

With `mutable: true`, Travels applies patches back to the original object so MobX, Vue, Pinia, or custom proxies can keep observing the same reference. It still generates forward and inverse patches for navigation and persistence.

Root replacements and primitive roots can require an immutable fallback. `enableAutoFreeze` cannot be combined with mutable mode. The [Mutable Mode Guide](/docs/guides/mutable-mode) explains every operation’s identity behavior.

## Automatic and manual history [#automatic-and-manual-history]

With `autoArchive: true`, every effective `setState()` creates an entry. With `autoArchive: false`, state updates remain pending until `archive()` or an operation that implicitly archives them.

```ts
const travels = createTravels({ x: 0, y: 0 }, { autoArchive: false });

travels.setState((draft) => { draft.x = 10; });
travels.setState((draft) => { draft.y = 20; });
travels.archive({ label: 'Move object' }); // One undo step
```

A root `transaction()` also groups updates, but additionally hides provisional states from Travels observers and rolls back Travels-tracked changes on failure.

## Branches and the redo boundary [#branches-and-the-redo-boundary]

```text
Initial ── A ── B ── C
              ▲
             back()
              │
              └── D   // A committed D discards redo entry C
```

`onBranchDiscard` receives the entries removed by this transition. Transactions report only redo entries visible before the root transaction, not branches created and discarded entirely inside provisional work.

## Retained window versus true baseline [#retained-window-versus-true-baseline]

`maxHistory` drops old patches as the timeline advances. The cursor is relative to the retained window, so it remains capped at that limit. `reset()` can still restore the instance’s true baseline even after older entries are trimmed.

`rebase()` is different: it intentionally discards all past and future history and makes current state the new baseline. See [History Lifecycle](/docs/concepts/history-lifecycle).

## What persistence stores [#what-persistence-stores]

`serialize()` creates one versioned value containing:

- current state;
- forward and inverse patch groups;
- current position;
- optional history metadata;
- the Travels history schema version.

`Travels.deserialize()` validates that value, and `restoreTravels()` creates a timeline from it atomically. No separate state/history alignment step is required.


# State Requirements (/docs/concepts/state-requirements)

Travels’ durable contract is deliberately smaller than JavaScript’s object model. It applies to current state, values retained in old patches, patch paths, and custom history metadata—not just the object passed to `createTravels()`.

## Preferred durable data [#preferred-durable-data]

Use plain objects, dense arrays, strings, finite numbers other than `-0`, booleans, and `null`. Patch paths must be Travels-accepted JSON Pointer strings or dense arrays of strings and finite non-negative integer indexes.

```ts
const state = {
  title: 'Draft',
  published: false,
  updatedAt: '2026-10-24T12:00:00.000Z',
  revision: 0,
  blocks: [{ id: 'intro', text: 'Hello' }],
};
```

Durable containers have normal writable, enumerable data properties and standard prototypes. Avoid accessors, hidden properties, custom own properties, non-extensible containers, array holes, and built-in subclasses. Standard frozen containers are recognized when `enableAutoFreeze` is enabled, but they are not a general durable-data recommendation for caller-created input.

## Compatibility matrix [#compatibility-matrix]

| Value | Runtime behavior | JSON persistence | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plain object | Supported | Supported | Preferred |
| Dense array | Supported | Supported | Preferred |
| Sparse, extended, or subclassed array | Limited or rejected by durable checks | Shape is not preserved | Normalize to a dense plain array |
| String, boolean, `null` | Supported | Supported | Preferred |
| Finite number other than `-0` | Supported | Supported | Preferred |
| `NaN`, infinities, `-0` | Supported in some in-memory paths | Becomes `null` or `0` | Normalize first |
| `bigint` | Supported in some in-memory paths | `JSON.stringify()` throws | Encode as a string |
| `undefined` | Patchable in memory | Removed from objects; array semantics differ | Use `null` |
| `Date` | Cloneable, not durable | Becomes a string through JSON | Store a timestamp or ISO string |
| `Map` / `Set` | Rejected in both runtime modes | Rejected at snapshot boundaries | Use records or dense arrays |
| Class or custom/null prototype | Not durable | Prototype and methods are lost | Store plain data or IDs |
| Function or symbol | Not durable | Dropped by JSON | Keep behavior outside state |
| Circular or shared graph identity | Not durable | Circular fails; shared identity is duplicated | Normalize to IDs |
| DOM node, ref, observable body | Not durable | Not serializable | Store outside Travels |
| `WeakMap` / `WeakSet` | Not supported | Not serializable | Store outside Travels |

Primitive roots work, but mutable mode cannot mutate a primitive in place and falls back to immutable replacement. Wrap a primitive in an object when stable root identity matters.

## Normalize collections at the boundary [#normalize-collections-at-the-boundary]

```ts
type Item = { id: string; title: string };

type LegacyState = {
  itemsById: Map<string, Item>;
  selectedIds: Set<string>;
  updatedAt: Date;
};

function normalize(state: LegacyState) {
  return {
    itemsById: Object.fromEntries(state.itemsById),
    selectedIds: Array.from(state.selectedIds),
    updatedAt: state.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}
```

Keep application-domain Map, Set, Date, or class views outside Travels and derive them from normalized state. Do not replay old collection-specific patch histories after conversion; materialize the authoritative current state, normalize it, and start a new baseline.

## Unsafe path keys [#unsafe-path-keys]

Mutative will not replay a change under a `__proto__` key or inside a value stored at a `constructor` key. Travels rejects such updates with `UNSUPPORTED_STATE`. Rename those keys before recording history. Root replacement has special handling in mutable and controlled-navigation paths; see the relevant guides before implementing in-place patch application.

## Static and runtime checks [#static-and-runtime-checks]

### Enforce the durable shape with `createPatchableTravels()` [#enforce-the-durable-shape-with-createpatchabletravels]

```ts
import { createPatchableTravels, type JsonValue } from 'travels';

const initial = {
  title: 'Draft',
  blocks: [] as Array<{ id: string; text: string }>,
} satisfies JsonValue;

const travels = createPatchableTravels(initial);
```

`PatchableInput<T>` performs a finite-depth, best-effort static check. TypeScript cannot prove every runtime property: `number` still includes `NaN`, infinities, and `-0`, and broad object types hide their contents. The strict factory therefore also validates its concrete initial value.

### Inspect a value directly [#inspect-a-value-directly]

```ts
import { findStateCompatibilityIssues } from 'travels';

const issues = findStateCompatibilityIssues(
  { createdAt: new Date(), selection: new Set(['a']) },
  { maxIssues: 20 }
);

for (const issue of issues) {
  console.warn(issue.code, issue.path, issue.message);
}
```

Issue codes identify circular/shared references, dates, functions, class instances, DOM nodes, Map/Set, bigint, non-JSON numbers, nonstandard array/object shapes, weak collections, symbols, and undefined values.

### Validate before or during serialization [#validate-before-or-during-serialization]

```ts
travels.assertPersistenceCompatible(); // Throws with path-specific diagnostics
const snapshot = travels.serialize({ strict: true });
```

`assertPersistenceCompatible()` checks current state, retained patch values and paths, and metadata. `serialize({ strict: true })` rejects any value that cannot round-trip through the documented JSON contract. Plain `serialize()` still returns detached data, but it does not normalize runtime-only values for you.

## Development diagnostics [#development-diagnostics]

Development builds scan initial and changed state plus retained patches and metadata for known hazards. `warnOnUnsupportedState: false` controls those warnings; it does not enable Map/Set or make invalid persistence safe. `onWarning` receives structured warning codes, and `onObserverError` isolates failures thrown by diagnostic or notification hooks.

The production package’s default entries avoid the full development scanner. Correctness boundaries such as strict serialization, restore validation, controlled patch validation, and Map/Set rejection remain explicit rather than depending on console warnings.


# Choosing Travels (/docs/getting-started/choosing-travels)

Travels is designed around a specific trade-off: spend work generating and applying patches to reduce retained history size and make complete timelines practical to persist. It is not intended to win every update-latency benchmark.

## Choose by workload [#choose-by-workload]

| Scenario | Recommended approach |
| --- | --- |
| Large state with localized edits | Travels: retained patches usually avoid repeated full-state copies |
| Long history that must survive reloads | Travels: one versioned snapshot includes state and history |
| Replayable operation logs or undo metadata | Travels: entries contain forward/inverse patches and metadata |
| Tiny state and a handful of local-only entries | A snapshot stack, Redux-undo, or Zundo may be simpler and faster |
| Replace most or all state on every edit | Measure both approaches; patches can approach snapshot cost |
| Collaborative conflict merging and concurrent users | A CRDT/OT system; Travels does not resolve conflicts by itself |

## Compare the costs [#compare-the-costs]

A snapshot history pays a state-copy cost for every entry and usually has cheap navigation. A patch history pays patch-generation and patch-application costs, while retaining only the changed operations for localized updates.

With Travels, immutable updates also use Mutative’s structural sharing. “Patch-based” does not mean every retained state is deep-cloned, and “smaller history” does not imply the lowest possible `setState()` latency.

Measure your actual workload across four dimensions:

1. Update latency and throughput.
2. Undo/redo and transaction latency.
3. Retained and serialized history size.
4. Save, restore, and semantic-validation cost.

The repository’s [benchmark suite](https://github.com/mutativejs/travels/tree/main/benchmarks) separates these concerns rather than presenting a single universal winner.

## Choose an ownership model [#choose-an-ownership-model]

### `createTravels()` [#createtravels]

Use this when Travels should receive and commit updates. It is the default choice for vanilla state, reducer-style state, and most new integrations.

- Immutable mode returns new state references.
- Mutable mode updates a live object for MobX, Vue, Pinia, and similar reactive owners.
- `setState()`, transactions, tracking controls, and `getControls()` are available.

### `createTravelJournal()` [#createtraveljournal]

Use this when another runtime already produces `nextState`, `patches`, and `inversePatches`. The external owner remains authoritative.

- Record an existing commit with `recordPatches()`.
- Apply undo/redo through the required synchronous `apply` callback.
- Avoid generating the same patches twice.
- Do not feed delegated navigation back into `recordPatches()`.

See the [Controlled Journal Guide](/docs/guides/controlled-journal) for the commit and failure boundaries.

## Choose an archive mode [#choose-an-archive-mode]

- **Automatic (`autoArchive: true`)**: each effective `setState()` call is one undo step. This is the default and the right starting point for most apps.
- **Manual (`autoArchive: false`)**: updates affect current state immediately, while `archive()` groups pending work into an entry. Use it for blur commits, drag gestures, or application-defined transactions.

For a single atomic operation with one final observer event, prefer `transaction()` over manually coordinating an archive.

## A practical decision checklist [#a-practical-decision-checklist]

Travels is likely a strong fit when most answers are yes:

- Is undo/redo a product feature rather than a debugging convenience?
- Are updates usually smaller than the complete state?
- Does history need metadata, persistence, or replay?
- Would a versioned snapshot simplify local-first storage?
- Do you need both immutable and reference-stable reactive integrations?

If your only requirement is a five-entry counter history in one component, a small local stack is probably enough.


# Installation (/docs/getting-started/installation)

## Requirements [#requirements]

- **Node.js 22 or newer** for server-side use and repository tooling.
- A **modern browser** with standard JavaScript and JSON APIs for browser applications.
- **Mutative 2** as Travels’ peer dependency.
- A bundler that defines `process.env.NODE_ENV`, or an explicit production Mutative browser build when loading ES modules without a bundler.

Travels ships ESM, CommonJS, UMD, and TypeScript declarations. The runtime support policy is documented under [Compatibility](/docs/reference/compatibility).

## Install the packages [#install-the-packages]

<Tabs items={["pnpm", "npm", "yarn"]}>
  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm add travels mutative
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npm install travels mutative
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn add travels mutative
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Install matching major versions: `travels@3` requires `mutative@^2.0.0`. Mutative 1 is not supported.

## Verify the installation [#verify-the-installation]

Create a small timeline and make one reversible edit:

```ts
import { createTravels } from 'travels';

const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 });

travels.setState((draft) => {
  draft.count += 1;
});

console.log(travels.getState()); // { count: 1 }
travels.back();
console.log(travels.getState()); // { count: 0 }
travels.forward();
console.log(travels.getState()); // { count: 1 }
```

`createTravels()` is the public factory. The exported `Travels` value is a persistence namespace, not a constructor; use `isTravels()` rather than `instanceof Travels` when detecting timelines.

## Optional official bindings [#optional-official-bindings]

Use the core API directly when you need framework-agnostic ownership, persistence, or custom integration. For a more idiomatic binding, install the matching v3 package:

| Binding | Purpose | Travels compatibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`use-travel`](https://github.com/mutativejs/use-travel) | React hooks and shared external-store timelines | `^3.0.0` |
| [`zustand-travel`](https://github.com/mutativejs/zustand-travel) | Zustand time-travel middleware | `^3.0.1` |

## Browser bundling note [#browser-bundling-note]

Mutative 2 targets ES2018 and selects development or production code through `process.env.NODE_ENV`. Vite, webpack, and comparable bundlers normally handle this. Without a bundler, use `mutative/dist/mutative.esm.production.min.mjs` or Mutative’s UMD build so the browser does not need a `process` global.

<Callout type="warn" title="Normalize durable state">
Plain objects, dense arrays, strings, finite numbers other than `-0`, booleans, and `null` form the durable state contract. Map and Set are rejected. Normalize dates, class instances, non-JSON numbers, functions, refs, and other runtime-only values before persistence. See [State Requirements](/docs/concepts/state-requirements).
</Callout>

## Next step [#next-step]

Follow the [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start) to add subscriptions, metadata, undo/redo controls, and persistence.


# Quick Start (/docs/getting-started/quick-start)

This guide builds a small document editor history. The same API works in vanilla JavaScript, TypeScript, and framework integrations.

## 1. Create a timeline [#1-create-a-timeline]

Pass the initial state and, optionally, the maximum number of retained patch entries:

```ts
import { createTravels } from 'travels';

type DocumentState = {
  title: string;
  blocks: Array<{ id: string; text: string }>;
};

const travels = createTravels<DocumentState>(
  { title: 'Untitled', blocks: [] },
  { maxHistory: 100 }
);
```

The initial state is the baseline at position `0`. `maxHistory` limits retained transitions, not the number of states returned by `getHistory()`; a window of 100 patches can expose 101 states.

## 2. Record an edit [#2-record-an-edit]

Use a draft recipe for the most natural update style:

```ts
travels.setState(
  (draft) => {
    draft.title = 'Product brief';
    draft.blocks.push({ id: 'intro', text: 'A reversible edit.' });
  },
  {
    label: 'Edit introduction',
    source: 'editor',
    timestamp: Date.now(),
  }
);
```

Travels commits one immutable state, stores forward and inverse patches, advances the cursor, and notifies subscribers. Metadata is attached to the history entry and included in persistence snapshots.

You can also provide a direct value or return a new state. Updaters must be synchronous:

```ts
travels.setState({ title: 'A new title', blocks: [] });
travels.setState(() => ({ title: 'Another title', blocks: [] }));
```

No-op updates that produce no patches do not create an entry or publish an event.

## 3. Observe committed changes [#3-observe-committed-changes]

Subscribe once and clean up when the owner is disposed:

```ts
const unsubscribe = travels.subscribe(
  ({ type, state, position, historyLength, metadata }) => {
    console.log({ type, state, position, historyLength, metadata });
  }
);

// Later, when the editor is destroyed:
unsubscribe();
```

Events are published after the timeline commits. Treat `event.state`, `event.patches`, and `event.metadata` as read-only. Do not synchronously call mutating Travels APIs from an observer; schedule follow-up work for a later task.

## 4. Add undo, redo, and navigation [#4-add-undo-redo-and-navigation]

```ts
if (travels.canBack()) travels.back();
if (travels.canForward()) travels.forward();

travels.back(2);      // Move back two entries
travels.forward(2);   // Move forward two entries
travels.go(0);        // Jump to the retained window start
travels.reset();      // Restore the instance baseline and clear the timeline
```

For UI components that need navigation but should not receive the full state-owning instance, use the cached controls facade:

```ts
const controls = travels.getControls();

controls.back();
controls.forward();
console.log(controls.position, controls.canBack(), controls.canForward());
```

A committed edit after undo discards the redo branch. Use `onBranchDiscard` when the application needs to observe that cleanup.

## 5. Group one logical operation [#5-group-one-logical-operation]

Use a transaction when several updates should become one undo step and observers should see only the settled result:

```ts
travels.transaction({ label: 'Revise document' }, () => {
  travels.setState((draft) => {
    draft.blocks.push({ id: 'revision', text: 'First revision' });
  });
  travels.setState((draft) => {
    draft.title = 'Revised brief';
  });
});
```

`batch()` is an alias for `transaction()`. Transaction callbacks must be synchronous; failures roll back changes made through Travels APIs. Learn more in [Transactions](/docs/guides/transactions).

## 6. Save and restore the timeline [#6-save-and-restore-the-timeline]

```ts
import { restoreTravels, Travels } from 'travels';

const encoded = JSON.stringify(travels.serialize());
localStorage.setItem('travels:quick-start', encoded);

// During a later startup:
const stored = localStorage.getItem('travels:quick-start');
if (stored) {
  const snapshot = Travels.deserialize<DocumentState>(stored, {
    validation: 'semantic',
  });
  const restored = restoreTravels(snapshot, { maxHistory: 100 });
  console.log(restored.getState());
}
```

The snapshot contains current state, retained forward and inverse patches, position, schema version, and optional metadata. `serialize()` returns detached data; it does not write to storage or call `JSON.stringify()` itself.

<Callout type="warn" title="Use semantic validation for unverified storage">
Structural validation is the fast default and checks schema and patch shape. Semantic validation additionally replays the reachable history in both directions. Use it for browser storage or other input that has not crossed a trusted verification boundary.
</Callout>

## 7. Keep exploring [#7-keep-exploring]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Connect React or another framework" href="/docs/integrations" />
  <Card title="Choose automatic or manual archives" href="/docs/guides/archive-mode" />
  <Card title="Build a production persistence adapter" href="/docs/persistence/storage-adapters" />
  <Card title="Review every instance method" href="/docs/reference/instance-methods" />
</Cards>


# Advanced Patterns (/docs/guides/advanced-patterns)

You can enhance Travels by wrapping its methods to add validation, permissions, logging, or other custom behavior.

## Table of Contents [#table-of-contents]

- [Intercepting and Modifying Operations](#intercepting-and-modifying-operations)
- [Adding Permission Checks](#adding-permission-checks)
- [Automatically Adding Metadata](#automatically-adding-metadata-to-state-changes)
- [Implementing Operation Logging and Auditing](#implementing-operation-logging-and-auditing)
- [Implementing Rate Limiting and Throttling](#implementing-rate-limiting-and-throttling)
- [Composing Multiple Wrappers](#composing-multiple-wrappers)
- [Detecting History Overflow](#detecting-history-overflow)
- [Common Patterns](#common-patterns)

## Intercepting and Modifying Operations [#intercepting-and-modifying-operations]

While `subscribe()` lets you observe state changes, it cannot prevent or modify operations. To add validation, permissions, or transform data before execution, wrap the Travels methods.

A `setState()` wrapper must keep both halves of the contract it replaces: pass the optional second `metadata` argument on, or the labels callers attach to history entries are lost, and let a function updater either mutate the draft or return a new state. Every example below does both.

`replaceStateWithoutHistory()` applies its update through `setState()`, so a `setState()` wrapper runs for it too. It clears the history unless that call throws, so a wrapper that blocks an update by returning early, as the validation and throttling examples do, keeps the old state but leaves nothing to undo. To block a replacement and keep the history, throw instead, as `withValidation()` under [Common Patterns](#common-patterns) does; `replaceStateWithoutHistory()` then throws the same error.

### Adding validation: [#adding-validation]

```typescript
const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 });

// Save the original method
const originalSetState = travels.setState.bind(travels);

// Wrap setState with validation
travels.setState = function (updater: any, metadata?: TravelMetadata) {
  // Validate direct values before Travels sees them
  if (typeof updater === 'object' && updater !== null) {
    // Validate
    if (updater.count < 0) {
      console.error('Count cannot be negative!');
      return; // Prevent execution
    }

    // Modify input - cap the count and stamp the change
    updater = {
      ...updater,
      count: Math.min(updater.count, 10),
      timestamp: Date.now(),
    };
  }

  // For function updaters, wrap to validate after execution
  if (typeof updater === 'function') {
    const wrappedUpdater = (draft: any) => {
      // Execute the original updater. It either mutates the draft or returns
      // a new state, so validate whichever one it produced.
      const result = updater(draft);
      const next = result === undefined ? draft : { ...result };

      // Validate after execution
      if (next.count > 10) {
        next.count = 10; // Fix invalid state
        console.warn('Count was capped at 10');
      }

      // Stamp the change
      next.timestamp = Date.now();

      // Pass a returned state on; a mutated draft needs no return value
      return result === undefined ? undefined : next;
    };

    originalSetState(wrappedUpdater, metadata);
    return;
  }

  // Execute for direct values
  originalSetState(updater, metadata);
} as any;

travels.setState({ count: 5 }); // ✅ Works
travels.setState({ count: -1 }); // ❌ Blocked
travels.setState({ count: 100 }); // ⚠️ Capped at 10

// Also works with function updaters, whether they mutate or return
travels.setState((draft) => {
  draft.count = 100; // Will be capped at 10
});
travels.setState(() => ({ count: 100 }), { label: 'max' }); // Capped, label kept
```

## Adding Permission Checks [#adding-permission-checks]

Wrap methods to verify permissions before allowing execution:

```typescript
const currentUser = { role: 'viewer' }; // Read-only user

// Prevent undo/redo for viewers
const originalBack = travels.back.bind(travels);
travels.back = function (amount?: number) {
  if (currentUser.role === 'viewer') {
    throw new Error('Permission denied: viewers cannot undo');
  }
  return originalBack(amount);
} as any;

// Same for other methods
const originalForward = travels.forward.bind(travels);
travels.forward = function (amount?: number) {
  if (currentUser.role === 'viewer') {
    throw new Error('Permission denied: viewers cannot redo');
  }
  return originalForward(amount);
} as any;

// Guard go() and reset() as well, or a viewer can still undo and redo with
// go() or return to the initial state with reset()
const originalGo = travels.go.bind(travels);
travels.go = function (position: number) {
  if (currentUser.role === 'viewer') {
    throw new Error('Permission denied: viewers cannot jump through history');
  }
  return originalGo(position);
} as any;

const originalReset = travels.reset.bind(travels);
travels.reset = function () {
  if (currentUser.role === 'viewer') {
    throw new Error('Permission denied: viewers cannot reset');
  }
  return originalReset();
} as any;
```

## Automatically Adding Metadata to State Changes [#automatically-adding-metadata-to-state-changes]

Wrap `setState` to inject metadata like timestamps or user IDs into the state. To label the history entry instead, add your fields to the `metadata` argument the wrapper forwards, which `getMetadata()` returns for each entry.

```typescript
const travels = createTravels<any>({ items: [] });
const currentUser = { id: 'user123' };

const originalSetState = travels.setState.bind(travels);

travels.setState = function (updater: any, metadata?: TravelMetadata) {
  // Handle direct value
  if (typeof updater === 'object' && updater !== null) {
    if (updater.items) {
      updater = {
        ...updater,
        items: updater.items.map((item: any) => ({
          ...item,
          timestamp: Date.now(),
          userId: currentUser.id,
          version: (item.version || 0) + 1,
        })),
      };
    }
    return originalSetState(updater, metadata);
  }

  // Handle function updaters
  if (typeof updater === 'function') {
    const wrappedUpdater = (draft: any) => {
      // Execute the original updater, keeping a state it returns
      const result = updater(draft);
      const next = result === undefined ? draft : result;

      // Add metadata after the update
      if (next.items) {
        next.items.forEach((item: any) => {
          if (!item.timestamp) {
            item.timestamp = Date.now();
            item.userId = currentUser.id;
            item.version = (item.version || 0) + 1;
          }
        });
      }
      return result;
    };
    return originalSetState(wrappedUpdater, metadata);
  }

  return originalSetState(updater, metadata);
} as any;

// Works with direct value
travels.setState({ items: [{ name: 'Task 1' }] });
// Result: { items: [{ name: 'Task 1', timestamp: ..., userId: ..., version: 1 }] }

// Also works with mutation
travels.setState((draft) => {
  draft.items.push({ name: 'Task 2' });
  // Metadata will be added automatically
});
```

## Implementing Operation Logging and Auditing [#implementing-operation-logging-and-auditing]

Wrap methods to record all operations before and after execution:

```typescript
const auditLog: any[] = [];

const originalSetState = travels.setState.bind(travels);

travels.setState = function (updater: any, metadata?: TravelMetadata) {
  // Log before
  auditLog.push({
    type: 'setState',
    timestamp: Date.now(),
    user: currentUser.id,
    before: travels.getState(),
  });

  // Execute
  const result = originalSetState(updater, metadata);

  // Log after
  auditLog.push({
    type: 'setState',
    timestamp: Date.now(),
    user: currentUser.id,
    after: travels.getState(),
  });

  return result;
} as any;
```

## Implementing Rate Limiting and Throttling [#implementing-rate-limiting-and-throttling]

Wrap methods to control how frequently they can be called:

```typescript
let lastCallTime = 0;
const throttleInterval = 100; // ms

const originalSetState = travels.setState.bind(travels);

travels.setState = function (updater: any, metadata?: TravelMetadata) {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (now - lastCallTime < throttleInterval) {
    console.warn('Too many updates, throttled');
    return;
  }
  lastCallTime = now;
  return originalSetState(updater, metadata);
} as any;
```

## Composing Multiple Wrappers [#composing-multiple-wrappers]

Create a reusable function that applies multiple enhancements:

```typescript
const currentUser = { id: 'user123', role: 'admin' };

// Helper function to wrap travels with multiple enhancers
function enhanceTravels<S>(
  travels: Travels<S>,
  config: {
    validation?: (state: any, draft?: any) => boolean | string;
    permissions?: (action: string) => boolean;
    logging?: boolean;
    metadata?: boolean;
  }
) {
  // Wrap setState
  if (config.validation || config.metadata || config.logging) {
    const original = travels.setState.bind(travels);
    travels.setState = function (updater: any, metadata?: TravelMetadata) {
      // Logging - before
      if (config.logging) {
        console.log('[setState] before:', travels.getState());
      }

      // Handle direct value
      if (typeof updater === 'object' && updater !== null) {
        // Validation for direct values
        if (config.validation) {
          const result = config.validation(updater);
          if (result !== true) {
            throw new Error(
              typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Validation failed'
            );
          }
        }

        // Add metadata for direct values
        if (config.metadata) {
          updater = {
            ...updater,
            _meta: { timestamp: Date.now(), user: currentUser.id },
          };
        }

        const res = original(updater, metadata);

        // Logging - after
        if (config.logging) {
          console.log('[setState] after:', travels.getState());
        }

        return res;
      }

      // Handle function updaters
      if (typeof updater === 'function') {
        const wrappedUpdater = (draft: any) => {
          // The updater mutates the draft or returns a new state
          const returned = updater(draft);
          const next = returned === undefined ? draft : { ...returned };

          // Validation for function updaters
          if (config.validation) {
            const result = config.validation(travels.getState(), next);
            if (result !== true) {
              throw new Error(
                typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Validation failed'
              );
            }
          }

          // Add metadata for function updaters
          if (config.metadata) {
            next._meta = { timestamp: Date.now(), user: currentUser.id };
          }

          return returned === undefined ? undefined : next;
        };

        const res = original(wrappedUpdater, metadata);

        // Logging - after
        if (config.logging) {
          console.log('[setState] after:', travels.getState());
        }

        return res;
      }

      return original(updater, metadata);
    } as any;
  }

  // Wrap navigation methods with permissions
  if (config.permissions) {
    const methods = ['back', 'forward', 'go', 'reset', 'archive', 'rebase'];
    methods.forEach((method) => {
      const original = (travels as any)[method]?.bind(travels);
      if (original) {
        (travels as any)[method] = function (...args: any[]) {
          if (!config.permissions!(method)) {
            throw new Error(`Permission denied: ${method}`);
          }
          return original(...args);
        };
      }
    });
  }

  return travels;
}

// Usage
const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 });
const enhanced = enhanceTravels(travels, {
  validation: (state, draft) => {
    const target = draft || state;
    if (target.count < 0) return 'Count cannot be negative';
    if (target.count > 100) return 'Count cannot exceed 100';
    return true;
  },
  permissions: (action) => {
    return currentUser.role !== 'viewer' || action === 'setState';
  },
  logging: true,
  metadata: true,
});

// Now works with both styles
enhanced.setState({ count: 50 }); // ✅ Direct value
enhanced.setState((draft) => {
  draft.count = 75;
}); // ✅ Mutation
```

## Detecting History Overflow [#detecting-history-overflow]

Use `subscribe()` to detect when history reaches the maximum limit:

```typescript
const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 }, { maxHistory: 5 });
const archive: any[] = [];

let lastPosition = 0;

travels.subscribe(({ position }) => {
  // Detect overflow: position stops growing
  if (position === lastPosition && position >= 5) {
    // Archive to external storage
    archive.push({
      state: travels.getState(),
      patches: travels.getPatches(),
      timestamp: Date.now(),
    });

    // You can save to localStorage, IndexedDB, or API
    localStorage.setItem('archive', JSON.stringify(archive));
  }

  lastPosition = position;
});
```

## Common Patterns [#common-patterns]

Here are some reusable wrapper patterns:

```typescript
// Pattern 1: Validation wrapper
function withValidation<S>(
  travels: Travels<S>,
  validator: (nextState: any) => boolean | string
) {
  const original = travels.setState.bind(travels);
  travels.setState = function (updater: any, metadata?: TravelMetadata) {
    // Handle direct value
    if (typeof updater === 'object' && updater !== null) {
      const result = validator(updater);
      if (result !== true) {
        throw new Error(
          typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Validation failed'
        );
      }
      return original(updater, metadata);
    }

    // Handle function updaters, validating the draft or the returned state
    if (typeof updater === 'function') {
      const wrapped = (draft: any) => {
        const returned = updater(draft);
        const result = validator(returned === undefined ? draft : returned);
        if (result !== true) {
          throw new Error(
            typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Validation failed'
          );
        }
        return returned;
      };
      return original(wrapped, metadata);
    }

    return original(updater, metadata);
  } as any;
  return travels;
}

// Pattern 2: Logging wrapper
function withLogging<S>(travels: Travels<S>) {
  const methods = ['setState', 'back', 'forward', 'reset', 'archive', 'rebase'];
  methods.forEach((method) => {
    const original = (travels as any)[method]?.bind(travels);
    if (original) {
      (travels as any)[method] = function (...args: any[]) {
        console.log(`[${method}] called with:`, args);
        const result = original(...args);
        console.log(`[${method}] result:`, travels.getState());
        return result;
      };
    }
  });
  return travels;
}

// Pattern 3: Permissions wrapper
function withPermissions<S>(
  travels: Travels<S>,
  checkPermission: (action: string) => boolean
) {
  const methods = [
    'setState',
    'back',
    'forward',
    'go',
    'reset',
    'archive',
    'rebase',
  ];
  methods.forEach((method) => {
    const original = (travels as any)[method]?.bind(travels);
    if (original) {
      (travels as any)[method] = function (...args: any[]) {
        if (!checkPermission(method)) {
          throw new Error(`Permission denied: ${method}`);
        }
        return original(...args);
      };
    }
  });
  return travels;
}

// Compose all wrappers
const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 });

withValidation(
  travels,
  (state) => state.count >= 0 || 'Count must be non-negative'
);
withLogging(travels);
withPermissions(travels, (action) => currentUser.role === 'admin');
```

## Back to Main Documentation [#back-to-main-documentation]

See the [main README](/docs) for basic usage, API reference, and getting started guide.


# Archive Mode (/docs/guides/archive-mode)

The archive mode defines when effective state changes become undoable history entries. It does not change when current state updates: pending manual edits are already visible in current state.

## Automatic archive — the default [#automatic-archive--the-default]

```ts
const travels = createTravels({ count: 0 });

travels.setState({ count: 1 }); // Entry 1
travels.setState({ count: 2 }); // Entry 2
travels.back();                 // count: 1
```

Use automatic mode when each call represents one complete user action. No-op updates do not create entries. Automatic timelines omit `archive()` and `canArchive()` at runtime and in TypeScript.

## Manual archive [#manual-archive]

```ts
const travels = createTravels(
  { title: '', description: '' },
  { autoArchive: false }
);

travels.setState((draft) => { draft.title = 'Brief'; });
travels.setState((draft) => { draft.description = 'Draft'; });

travels.canArchive(); // true
travels.archive({ label: 'Create brief' });
travels.canArchive(); // false

travels.back(); // Returns to the state before both edits
```

Manual mode is useful for:

- committing a field group on blur or save;
- treating a drag gesture as one step;
- letting an external form manager define the undo boundary;
- composing updates without immediately exposing separate undo entries.

## Metadata selection [#metadata-selection]

`archive(metadata?)` accepts the entry’s final metadata. If omitted, Travels uses the latest metadata supplied to pending `setState()` calls.

```ts
travels.setState(updateTitle, { source: 'title-field' });
travels.setState(updateBody, { source: 'body-field' });
travels.archive({ label: 'Edit document', source: 'editor' });
```

Keep metadata durable when persisting history.

## Navigation implicitly archives pending work [#navigation-implicitly-archives-pending-work]

Calling `back()`, `forward()`, or `go()` with pending manual changes archives them as part of navigation so cursor positions remain meaningful. The archive and movement commit as one observable transition.

```ts
travels.setState(updateDraft);
travels.back(); // Pending work is archived, then navigation occurs
```

In Travels 3 this publishes one `go` event and advances `getRevision()` once. Persist from every committed event, not only from `archive` events.

## Transactions in manual mode [#transactions-in-manual-mode]

A root `transaction()` archives when it commits. Changes already pending before the transaction join its entry, so undo reverts them together. Transaction metadata takes precedence; without it, the latest pending update metadata is used.

A transaction whose own updates cancel out can leave earlier pending work pending. For the full matrix, see [Transactions](/docs/guides/transactions).

## Cancelled pending changes [#cancelled-pending-changes]

Pending changes that cancel each other out are dropped instead of retained as a meaningful undo entry. `archive()` can still publish an `archive` event for the archive operation even when no net state change remains. Navigation counts positions with the pending entry in place, so its behavior follows the navigation contract rather than simply deleting the entry.

## Automatic versus manual [#automatic-versus-manual]

| Behavior | Automatic | Manual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Effective `setState()` creates an entry | Immediately | Only when archived |
| Current state updates | Immediately | Immediately |
| `archive()` / `canArchive()` | Absent | Available |
| Typical boundary | One update call | Application-defined gesture or commit |
| Root transaction | One grouped entry | Also archives earlier pending work |

Start with automatic mode. Choose manual mode only when the application has a clear commit boundary; an update that is never archived cannot be navigated as an independent completed step.


# Controlled Journal (/docs/guides/controlled-journal)

`createTravelJournal()` is the adapter API for a runtime that already owns and commits state. It lets that runtime hand an existing forward/inverse patch pair to Travels without rerunning the update recipe or routing navigation around the owner's validation and subscription pipeline.

Use `createTravels()` instead when Travels itself should own state updates. Restore serialized journal history with `restoreTravelJournal(snapshot, { apply })`; the snapshot state and timeline are accepted as one atomic input.

## Data flow [#data-flow]

An external commit has one authoritative path:

1. The owner produces `nextState`, `patches`, and `inversePatches` for one transition.
2. The owner commits `nextState` through its normal state path.
3. In the same synchronous commit boundary, the adapter calls `journal.recordPatches(nextState, { patches, inversePatches, metadata })`.
4. Travels detaches the patch pair and metadata, updates its cursor and retained history, then publishes one `recordPatches` event.

`recordPatches()` requires a non-empty patch pair when the supplied state reference changes. It validates patch structure and supported patch values, but does not replay the pair to prove that it transforms the previous state into the supplied state. That relationship is the adapter's responsibility; replay validation here would duplicate the external runtime's work and defeat the single-generation integration path.

Owners that cannot roll back a published commit can call `assertTravelHistoryEntryRecordable({ patches, inversePatches })` before step 2. The preflight uses the same structural validation and detached-value rules as `recordPatches()` without changing journal state.

Patch groups and metadata are cloned before Travels retains them. The supplied state remains the external owner's state reference and is not cloned.

## Navigation and reset contract [#navigation-and-reset-contract]

`back()`, `forward()`, `go()`, and `reset()` compose the necessary patches and invoke the required `apply` callback:

```ts
const journal = createTravelJournal(authoritativeState, {
  apply(transition) {
    authoritativeState = commitThroughOwner(transition.patches);
    return authoritativeState;
  },
});
```

The callback receives:

- `state`: the state Travels knew before navigation;
- `patches`: the composed forward transition to commit;
- `inversePatches`: the composed rollback transition;
- `fromPosition` and `toPosition`: the cursor movement.

`reset()` also describes its return to the baseline as patches. When the current state and the baseline are both plain objects, or both arrays, those patches overwrite the root's entries and keep the root itself, so an owner can apply them in place, for example with Mutative's `apply(state, patches, { mutable: true })`. When the root kinds differ, the state is not an object, or either root has an own `__proto__` key, which no patch path can name, the transition replaces the root with one `{ op: 'replace', path: [] }` patch. An owner that applies transitions in place must handle that patch itself, as it must for root replacements it recorded through `recordPatches()`: Mutative 2 throws for a root replacement applied in place, and Mutative 1 skipped it, which left the owner's state unchanged while the journal moved.

The transition contains detached patch operations and values, so accidental callback mutation cannot rewrite retained history. The callback should still treat them as read-only because changing them before the owner commits would change the requested navigation. Patch values that contain functions, accessors, `WeakMap`/`WeakSet`, custom class instances, array subclasses, or another value that cannot be cloned without changing its runtime type are rejected with `UNCLONEABLE_PATCH_VALUE`; controlled journals should retain primitives, plain objects, plain arrays, or `Date` values. `apply` must finish synchronously and return the state actually committed by the owner. A thrown error, uncloneable transition, or Promise-like result does not advance the cursor, replace the retained state reference, or change history.

In development builds Travels also scans the returned state for `Map` and `Set`, and an unsupported state is rejected with the same atomicity: the cursor, retained state reference, and history are unchanged. That scan is proportional to the whole state, so production builds skip it and pay nothing per navigation. It is a diagnostic that tells an owner early which transition introduced an unsupported value, not the guarantee that keeps persistence sound: `serialize()`, `rebase()`, and `getHistorySnapshot()` validate the state in every build, and controlled patch values are validated in every build, so an unsupported value can never reach retained history or a persisted snapshot. Develop against a development build to keep the early signal. Travels cannot undo mutations or other side effects the external owner already performed before failing.

The owner must suppress normal commit recording while applying delegated navigation or reset. Feeding those changes back into `recordPatches()` would create a new entry instead of moving or clearing the existing timeline. Travels rejects every journal mutation attempted synchronously from `apply` with `REENTRANT_MUTATION`; reads remain available to the owner callback.

Set `autoArchive: false` when several external commits should become one undo step. Each `recordPatches()` call updates the pending current state; `archive(metadata?)` composes the pending patch groups, and `canArchive()` reports whether any work is pending. Archiving changes only journal history and does not invoke `apply` because the external owner already committed the state. When navigation implicitly archives pending work, the archive and cursor move commit as one observable navigation transition; a failed `apply` leaves the pending archive, revision, and subscriptions untouched.

## Public surface [#public-surface]

The returned `TravelJournal` exposes only journal-safe operations:

- external commit ingress: `recordPatches()`;
- navigation: `back()`, `forward()`, `go()`, `reset()`, `canBack()`, and `canForward()`;
- reads: `getState()`, `getHistory()`, `getHistorySnapshot()`, `getPosition()`, `getPatches()`, `getMetadata()`, `getHistoryEntries()`, `assertPersistenceCompatible()`, and `serialize()`;
- lifecycle: `subscribe()` and `rebase()`;
- manual journals only: `archive()` and `canArchive()`.

The facade is a frozen read-only capability object in every build; its methods cannot be replaced at runtime.

State-owning operations (`setState()`, transactions, `replaceStateWithoutHistory()`, tracking controls, and `getControls()`) are absent from both the public type and the runtime facade. `rebase()` is the safe way to clear retained history while keeping the current external state as the new baseline; `reset()` instead asks the external owner to restore the existing baseline.

## Failure boundaries [#failure-boundaries]

Travels makes each journal mutation internally atomic: malformed, empty, or one-sided patch pairs, unsafe paths, unsupported patch/state values, metadata cloning failures, and controlled navigation failures do not partially change journal state or history. Controlled patch ingress uses the same accessor-safe structural normalization as persisted history.

The external owner and Travels are still two components. If the owner has already published a commit and `recordPatches()` then fails, Travels cannot roll that external commit back automatically. Generate patches through a trusted producer, keep metadata cloneable, and call `recordPatches()` before publishing external notifications when the owner supports that ordering. An adapter that cannot roll back should recover explicitly, for example by rebasing the journal at the authoritative state or switching to its documented compatibility fallback.

Observer failures happen after a successful journal commit and follow the normal `onObserverError` contract; they do not roll the transition back.

## Event compatibility [#event-compatibility]

A successful external commit emits `TravelsEvent` with type `recordPatches`. Navigation emits `go`, including calls made through `back()` or `forward()`. The event patch groups describe only that event's transition.

`TravelsEvent['type']` intentionally remains open to future minor-release event names. Consumers should handle known operations and keep a `default` branch instead of asserting exhaustiveness with `never`. Applications using only `createTravels()` do not receive `recordPatches` at runtime.


# Error Handling (/docs/guides/error-handling)

Travels separates operation errors, persistence decoding errors, non-fatal warnings, and observer failures. Match stable `code` values rather than production error message text.

## Operation errors [#operation-errors]

`TravelsError` extends `Error`; `TravelsTypeError` extends `TypeError`. Both expose a stable `code` and optional `cause`.

```ts
import { TravelsError, TravelsTypeError } from 'travels';

try {
  travels.transaction(updateDocument);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TravelsError || error instanceof TravelsTypeError) {
    console.error(error.code, error.cause);
  }
  throw error;
}
```

Common codes include:

| Code | Typical meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ASYNC_CALLBACK` | An updater or transaction returned asynchronous work. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | Factory or restore options are incompatible or malformed. |
| `INVALID_OPERATION` | The requested operation is not allowed for that capability or state. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_STATE` | State or a patch path violates the runtime state contract. |
| `PERSISTENCE_INCOMPATIBLE` | State, patches, paths, or metadata are not durable. |
| `HISTORY_REPLAY_FAILED` | A retained patch could not be applied during navigation or reconstruction. |
| `TRANSACTION_FAILED` | The atomic operation failed; inspect `cause`. |
| `REENTRANT_MUTATION` | A synchronous observer or controlled callback attempted a nested mutation. |
| `INVALID_PATCH_ENTRY` / `EMPTY_PATCH_ENTRY` | A controlled patch pair is malformed or missing required operations. |
| `UNCLONEABLE_PATCH_VALUE` | A controlled patch value cannot be detached safely. |
| `CONTROLLED_JOURNAL_REQUIRED` | An operation requires a controlled journal. |
| `CONTROLLED_OPERATION_UNAVAILABLE` | A state-owning capability was requested from a journal. |

Use `onError` for wrapped core operation failures, especially when coordinating nested transactions. Keep local `try/catch` around actions whose errors the UI must handle synchronously; do not assume a hook replaces the thrown error.

## Persistence errors [#persistence-errors]

`TravelsPersistenceError` covers decoding, migration, and validation:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PARSE_ERROR` | JSON input could not be parsed. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` | The snapshot schema version is not supported. |
| `INVALID_SCHEMA` | Snapshot fields, metadata, or position are malformed. |
| `INVALID_PATCHES` | Patch containers, operations, paths, or values are invalid. |
| `INVALID_HISTORY` | Semantic replay or reversibility failed. |
| `MIGRATION_FAILED` | The migration callback failed or returned an invalid/asynchronous result. |
| `FALLBACK_FAILED` | Recovery failed or produced an invalid/asynchronous result. |

Entry-specific semantic failures can also expose `entryIndex` and `direction`. See [Migration and Recovery](/docs/persistence/migration-and-recovery).

## Warnings [#warnings]

`onWarning` receives non-fatal diagnostics with stable codes:

```ts
const travels = createTravels(initialState, {
  onWarning({ code, message }) {
    diagnostics.log({ code, message });
  },
});
```

Warning codes include `HISTORY_DISABLED`, `HISTORY_DISCARDED`, `HISTORY_TRIMMED`, `INVALID_POSITION`, `MUTABLE_FALLBACK`, `MUTABLE_ROOT_REPLACEMENT`, `PERSISTENCE_COMPATIBILITY`, and `POSITION_CLAMPED`.

Without the hook, warnings are written to the console only in development. Disabling compatibility warnings does not disable runtime correctness checks.

## Observer failures [#observer-failures]

Errors thrown by listeners, devtools, branch-discard hooks, error/warning hooks, or compatibility checks after commit are routed to `onObserverError` when configured. They do not interrupt other observers or roll back an already committed transition.

```ts
const travels = createTravels(initialState, {
  onObserverError({ source, error }) {
    reportError({ source, error });
  },
});
```

Observer Promises are not awaited, but rejected Promises are isolated and reported. The application remains responsible for actual asynchronous side-effect recovery.

## Recovery by boundary [#recovery-by-boundary]

- **Invalid caller input:** fix options or state before constructing the timeline; do not continue with a partially initialized owner.
- **Failed transaction:** Travels rolls back writes made through its APIs. Application side effects and direct mutable-store writes need separate handling.
- **Unverified persisted history:** use `validation: 'semantic'` and a known-safe `fallback` before restore.
- **Controlled ingress:** call `assertTravelHistoryEntryRecordable()` before an external commit when the owner cannot roll back a published change.
- **Failed controlled `apply`:** Travels does not advance its own cursor, but cannot undo side effects already performed by the external owner.
- **Replay failure in mutable mode:** writes made before the failing patch can remain. Prefer semantic validation before restoring unverified snapshots.

For integrity and tamper resistance, verify encoded bytes outside Travels before deserialization; replay consistency alone does not prove provenance.

# Mutable Mode (/docs/guides/mutable-mode)

Mutable mode makes Travels play nicely with observable state libraries (MobX, Vue's `reactive`, Pinia stores, etc.) that rely on **stable object references** to notify subscribers. Instead of replacing the entire state object on every update, Travels mutates the original object in place while still recording JSON Patches for undo/redo.

Use this guide to decide when to enable `mutable: true`, understand how it works internally, and apply it safely in production apps.

## When You Should Enable Mutable Mode [#when-you-should-enable-mutable-mode]

- You hand Travels the same object that your UI library observes and you cannot replace that reference without breaking reactivity (MobX stores, Vue/Pinia stores, custom proxies).
- You want undo/redo without extra `setState({...state})` copies or garbage-collection churn.
- You batch updates with `autoArchive: false` but still expect the live store reference to update immediately.

Stick with the default immutable mode when you already replace references (React/Redux style reducers, Zustand, etc.) or when you prefer structural sharing for diffing.

## Enabling Mutable Mode [#enabling-mutable-mode]

```ts
import { createTravels } from 'travels';

const store = reactive({ count: 0 }); // Vue/Pinia example
const travels = createTravels(store, { mutable: true });

travels.setState((draft) => {
  draft.count += 1; // Mutates `store` in place
});
```

After this ordinary draft update, `travels.getState()` still returns `store`. Effective changes still produce patches, but explicit root replacements and primitive roots can change the root reference as described below.

## How It Works Under the Hood [#how-it-works-under-the-hood]

1. `createTravels` keeps the object you pass as the live state and stores a detached baseline copy for `reset()`, using `structuredClone()` when possible and a custom deep-clone fallback otherwise.
2. Each ordinary object-root draft update runs through Mutative's `create(...)` to generate patches/inverse patches. Those patches are immediately applied back to the live object via `apply(..., { mutable: true })`, preserving its reference. Explicit root replacements instead use an immutable fallback.
3. Navigation commands (`back`, `forward`, `go`) reuse the stored patches. `reset()` instead computes a fresh diff back to that baseline copy so it can restore the original data without replaying every history step.
4. If a history step replaces the entire root (patch path `[]` with `op: 'replace'`), Travels falls back to immutable assignment for that jump to guarantee correctness.

The full implementation lives in `src/travels.ts` and is exercised by `test/mutable-mode.test.ts` and `test/primitive-edge-cases.test.ts`.

## Restoring Persisted History Into a Live Store [#restoring-persisted-history-into-a-live-store]

`restoreTravels(snapshot)` restores a detached copy of the snapshot state, which would break reactivity for a store that is already observed. Pass the observed object as `target` instead:

```ts
import { reactive } from 'vue';
import { restoreTravels, Travels } from 'travels';

const store = reactive({ count: 0 });
const snapshot = Travels.deserialize<typeof store>(stored, {
  validation: 'semantic',
});
const travels = restoreTravels(snapshot, { mutable: true, target: store });

travels.getState() === store; // true
travels.back(); // Localized patches mutate `store`; root replacements can reassign it
```

Travels overwrites `target` in place with a copy of `snapshot.state` before it records anything, so the live object and the restored patch history always start from the same data. The snapshot itself is never mutated. `target` requires `mutable: true` and must have the same root kind (plain object or array) as the snapshot state, and neither root may have an own `__proto__` key; it is rejected with `INVALID_OPTION` otherwise.

## Behavior by Operation [#behavior-by-operation]
